question: Prediction of conversion from MCI to AD within 3 years, from baseline data, among ADNI MCI participants. Both models are multimodal and share the clinical/cognitive channel. P-243 (Wu et al., Age Ageing 2023) uses eight LASSO-selected variables: ADAS11, RAVLT immediate and learning, FAQ and mPACCtrailsB plus FreeSurfer fusiform, middle temporal and intracranial volumes. P-81 (Cao et al., Neurobiol Dis 2023) uses CDR-SB, logical memory delayed recall, MMSE, mPACCdigit and mPACCtrailsB plus age and whole-brain FDG-PET. The imaging channel differs (sMRI volumes vs FDG-PET), but P-81 also prints models without imaging (cognitive scores, with and without age), so a same-channel comparison exists on its side. Cohort, instruments, model and validation differ, which condition 1 allows. The ledger record still names P-320 for claim_b; the figure (0.785) is P-81's.

figures.P-243: AdaBoost (logistic-regression base) on the 8 LASSO variables, 627 MCI (269 converters / 358 stable). Held-out 30% test set: AUC 0.89 (accuracy 0.83, recall 0.71), no interval printed. The test split's class counts are not printed; at the cohort ratio about 81 converters / 107 stable of 188. Hanley-McNeil: Q1 = 0.89/1.11 = 0.8018, Q2 = 2(0.89^2)/1.89 = 0.8382, SE = sqrt([0.89*0.11 + 80*(0.8018-0.7921) + 106*(0.8382-0.7921)]/(81*107)) = 0.0258, 95% CI [0.840, 0.941]. Validation (5-fold CV within the 70%, about 188/251): AUC 0.91 +/- 0.03, Hanley-McNeil CI [0.880, 0.940]; fold-based 0.91 +/- 2.776*0.03/sqrt(5) = [0.873, 0.947].
figures.P-81: 5-fold CV over 257 MCI (93 converters / 164 stable), mean +/- fold SD (Table 3). PET + age + CS (the recorded model): AUC 0.7849 +/- 0.0963, Hanley-McNeil Q1 = 0.646, Q2 = 0.690, SE = 0.0314, CI [0.723, 0.846]. CS + age (no imaging, P-81's highest AUC): 0.8004, SE 0.0305, CI [0.741, 0.860]. PET + CS: 0.7983, CI [0.738, 0.858]. CS alone: 0.7496, CI [0.685, 0.815]. PET alone: 0.6102.

matched_figure_check: No matched figure. P-243 uses no PET and prints no cognitive-only model; P-81 prints no sMRI-volume model. The closest same-channel figure is P-81's best model without imaging (CS + age, AUC 0.800, CI [0.741, 0.860]), and it does not close the gap: P-243's 0.89 lies above its upper bound, and 0.800 lies below P-243's lower bound 0.840. Every P-81 variant (0.61-0.80) lies below 0.840. P-243's sub-interval AUCs (0.98 at 0-6 months down to 0.80 at 24-36 months) regroup the same 3-year test set by time to conversion; they are not the other paper's condition.
performance_validity: Neither study meets the exclusion. The compared figures are 0.89 (held-out test) and 0.785 (5-fold CV); P-243's 0.98 is a 0-6-month sub-interval, not the compared figure, and P-81's 1.0 values are its CN vs AD pretraining, which the authors attribute to scores used to define AD. Checked against P-243 Tables 1-2 and P-81 Tables 2-3.

candidate_explanations.difference: Cognitive instruments: P-243's strongest predictors are FAQ, mPACCtrailsB, RAVLT immediate and ADAS11; P-81 has no FAQ, ADAS or RAVLT and uses CDR-SB, logical memory, MMSE and two mPACC variants.
candidate_explanations.quote: Generally, scores from the FAQ, ADAS11 and Modiﬁed Preclinical Alzheimer Cognitive Composite with Trails test (mPACCtrailsB) ranked top 3.

candidate_explanations.difference: Imaging channel: three FreeSurfer volumes (P-243) vs whole-brain FDG-PET (P-81). P-81 shows PET adds little to cognitive scores, so this is not shown to carry the gap.
candidate_explanations.quote: Neurocognitive scores predicted better than FDG-PET per se, but the best model was a combination of FDG-PET, age, and neurocognitive data, yielding an AUC of 0.785 ± 0.096 and a balanced accuracy of 0.733 ± 0.098.

candidate_explanations.difference: Cohort selection and class balance: 627 MCI from ADNI-1/GO/2/3 with 43% converters, requiring 3-year follow-up and excluding bidirectional changes, vs 257 MCI from ADNI-1/2/GO with 36% converters, restricted to participants with FDG-PET within two months of baseline.
candidate_explanations.quote: The inclusion criteria require the recruited participants to have a 3D whole-brain FDG-PET scan taken within two months of baseline diagnosis

candidate_explanations.difference: Label definition: P-243 requires a 3-year follow-up and excludes participants with bidirectional diagnostic changes; P-81 labels those who do not convert within three years as stable without a stated follow-up requirement.
candidate_explanations.quote: The inclusion criteria of the samples in this study were: (i) diagnosed with MCI at baseline; (ii) had a follow-up time of 3 years; (iii) had outcome (cognitive status) information. Participants diagnosed with bidirectional changes during follow-up were excluded

candidate_explanations.difference: Model and validation: LASSO selection plus Bayesian-tuned AdaBoost over logistic regression, chosen among many models and fusion strategies on 5-fold CV and evaluated once on a 30% held-out set (P-243), vs a 3D CNN plus dense layers for the scores, trained on CN vs AD and carried over to MCI conversion by zero-shot transfer (the Table 3 figures), evaluated by 5-fold CV on 257 subjects (P-81).
candidate_explanations.quote: Finally, the test set (30%) was used to assess the per-formance of optimal model.

candidate_explanations.difference: P-81's own warning that such comparisons can be confounded by prediction window, data heterogeneity and reporting bias.
candidate_explanations.quote: However, interpretation of performance metrics needs to be made with caution. Differences in performance could be due to differences many factors.

reason: Both papers predict 3-year MCI-to-AD conversion in ADNI with multimodal models that share the cognitive-score channel. P-243's AUC 0.89 [0.840, 0.941] and P-81's 0.785 [0.723, 0.846] each lie outside the other's Hanley-McNeil interval (z = 0.105/sqrt(0.0258^2 + 0.0314^2) = 2.59), and P-81's best model without imaging (0.800 [0.741, 0.860]) does not close the gap. Neither paper reports a result under the other's condition, and neither is near ceiling. Sensitivity: with P-81's fold SD (t, 4 df) its interval widens to [0.665, 0.904] and contains 0.89, but 0.785 still lies outside P-243's fold-based validation interval [0.873, 0.947], so the one-directional criterion holds. Cognitive instruments (FAQ and ADAS in P-243 only), imaging channel, cohort, label definition and validation design are candidate explanations; neither paper shows any of them to be sufficient. Both cohorts come from ADNI, so subjects may overlap in part.

quotes.quote: Finally, a total of 627 patients with baseline MCI were screened, of whom 269 patients progressed to AD at a 3-year follow-up and 358 patients remained MCI.

Therefore, the AdaBoost model based on logistic regression is taken as the ﬁnal optimal model, and the accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score and AUC of the ﬁnal model on the test set are 0.83, 0.82, 0.71, 0.76 and 0.89, respectively.
Eight variables were selected by LASSO, that is, ADAS11, RAVLT_immediate, RAVLT_learning, Func-tional Activities Questionnaire (FAQ), Fusiform, MidTemp, ICV and mPACCtrailsB.
